gap: No result ChatGPT got says that nextpit measured the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at about 30 dB while charging at about 260 W in its quiet charging mode. They also don't say that The Technology Man's 37 dB readings for the BLUETTI AC180 and DJI Power 1000 V2 were only about 1 dB above the background noise in his room, so those readings can't show which unit is quieter.
standout_why: I compared this against the cited rival pages (thepowerstationguide.com noise guide, 2026-10-09; voltandvalley.com 'Are Portable Power Stations Loud?', 2026-10-17; powerstationgeek.com noise ratings, 2026-08-13) and our own current page. None of them has a measured figure for the Jackery 1000 v2 while charging. thepowerstationguide and voltandvalley give only Jackery's ≤22 dB claim, and volt&valley says it measured nothing itself. powerstationgeek has no Jackery, DJI V2, AC180 or C1000 Gen 2 figure, only 'sustained load' readings with no wattage or distance given. Our page and all seven ChatGPT answers label the Jackery quiet mode 'claimed / independently unverified'. None of them reports Notebookcheck's 45 dB for the C1000 Gen 2, or that The Technology Man's 37 dB readings sit at his room's background level.
decides: The Jackery 1000 v2 moves from 'claim only' to 'measured quiet mode'. nextpit got about 30 dB at about 260 W, a rate that would fill 1,070 Wh in roughly 4 to 4.5 h, close to the AC180 Silent mode's 283 W and 4.5 h. That makes it a measured contender for overnight bedroom charging, not just a footnote. The figures still come from different reviewers, rooms and (for nextpit) an unstated distance, so the page should not crown the Jackery quieter than the AC180. It should say that both have measured quiet modes near room noise. For fast charging, DJI Power 1000 V2 stays the pick: The Technology Man measured 37 dB at over 1,400 W, at background level. Two reviewers measured the Anker C1000 Gen 2 at full speed, 42 dB (The Technology Man) and 45 dB (Notebookcheck), and both put it louder than the DJI.

findings.label: Noise while charging in quiet charging mode (nextpit measurement)
findings.value: about 30 dB at about 260 W charge
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 im Test (nextpit, Thomas Kern, 2024-09-20)
findings.note: Quote: 'Zumindest für den Ladeprozess bietet Jackery in der App einen „leisen Lademodus“. In dieser Einstellung messen wir nur noch eine Lautstärke von etwa 30 dB… Im Test wird die Jackery-Powerstation mit etwa 260 W geladen.' The photo caption shows a sound meter during charging. Distance is not stated. German review, so probably a 230 V EU unit. Our arithmetic: 1,070 Wh / 260 W ≈ 4.1 h before charging losses.

findings.label: Noise in normal charging and discharging (nextpit measurement)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 im Test (nextpit, Thomas Kern, 2024-09-20)
findings.note: Quote: 'Leider ist die Explorer beim Be- und Entladen deutlich hörbar. In der Praxis messen wir eine Lautstärke von etwa 47 dB.' The review gives no mode, wattage or distance for this reading, and says the value depends heavily on distance.

findings.label: Measured time to full on mains (nextpit)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 im Test (nextpit, Thomas Kern, 2024-09-20)
findings.note: Quote: 'Im Praxistest war die Powerstation nach gerade mal 50 Minuten vollgeladen.' The next sentence gives 1,400 W mains charging (emergency mode), so this was probably the fast mode, not quiet mode. That is our inference; the text does not say so.

findings.label: Noise while charging in Silent mode (The Technology Man)
findings.value: about 37 dB at 1 m, 'just 1dB above background noise'
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Review | Best 1800W Power Station Solar Generator? (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2023-09-07)
findings.note: Room background was therefore about 36 dB, so 37 dB is the floor of this setup, not a figure to rank against other reviewers. No wattage is stated for Silent mode in this review.

findings.label: Noise while charging at full speed (The Technology Man)
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Review | Best 1800W Power Station Solar Generator? (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2023-09-07)
findings.note: Turbo/full-speed charging. The reviewer measured a full charge in 'almost exactly one hour' and says this was about 10 dB quieter than an EcoFlow Delta 2 at full speed.

findings.label: Noise while charging at full speed (The Technology Man)
findings.value: about 37 dB at 1 m at over 1,400 W
findings.source_title: This Compact Power Station Can Output 2600W – DJI Power 1000 V2 Review (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2025-08-08)
findings.note: Quote: 'One metre away my dB meter barely picked up anything over and above background noise – I measured around 37dB.' Fast mode, over 1,400 W. Measured 80% in under 40 min and full in under 53 min. Standard mode (about 600 W) was not measured.

findings.label: Noise while charging at full speed (The Technology Man)
findings.value: about 42 dB at 1 m at 1,600 W UltraFast
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2025-11-04)
findings.note: The reviewer says the fans vary their speed, which makes them more noticeable. At 600 W 'Silent' it was 'a lot quieter but not silent' (no dB given). At 200 W the fans were off. Measured full charge 47 min at about 20 °C.

findings.label: Noise at fast AC charging and high output (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but...: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2025-12-21, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Quote: 'a good 45 dB (measured from a distance of 1 m) at higher power output and fast AC charging'. The exact wattage is not stated. Measured AC charge just under 55 min without Boost. A second named reviewer at a different site, 3 dB louder than The Technology Man's reading.

unsourced: A measured dB figure for the DJI Power 1000 V2 in Standard (about 600 W) charging mode: The Technology Man measured only Fast mode, drohnen.de repeats DJI's 26 dB with no attribution, and I found no Notebookcheck review of the V2 (only launch news).
A measured dB figure for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at its 600 W 'Silent' setting: The Technology Man describes it but gives no number, and Notebookcheck gives none.

A named-reviewer dB figure for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus or DELTA 3 while AC charging: StorageReview's 30 dB at under 600 W and 40 dB at 1,200 W match EcoFlow's spec table and are not labelled as measured; T3 and The Solar Lab give no dB; The Technology Man reviewed only the DELTA 3 Max Plus.
The measuring distance for nextpit's 30 dB and 47 dB Jackery readings: the review does not state it.
Any measured charging noise for the ALLPOWERS P1800's 400 W silent mode.

RTINGS-style or lab measurements of the same units in one room: I found no single reviewer who measured more than one of these candidates in the same setup, apart from The Technology Man (AC180, DJI V2, C1000 Gen 2).
